trailhead: Cedar Creek Trailhead (Sandy Butte-Cedar Creek Road #200)
trailheadDirection: From the Cedar Creek Trailhead at the end of Sandy Butte-Cedar Creek Road #200, ~4.25 miles west of Mazama off SR-20
From Winthrop, west on SR-20 about 18 miles to FR 5310-200, about half a mile east of the Klipchuck Campground turnoff, then to the trailhead by the gravel pit at the road's end (~3,000 ft)

From the Climbers Bivouac trailhead (3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain, reached via FR-90/FR-83/FR-81/FR-830 from Cougar), the route starts on the signed Ptarmigan Trail #216A through open forest.
From the Cold Springs / South Climb Trailhead (~5,600 ft, end of FR-8040 north of Trout Lake), via South Climb Trail #183

From Trout Lake, drive Mount Adams Road north to the V intersection with FR-23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto FR-80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto FR-8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the old Cold Springs Camp; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.
North from Trout Lake via Mt. Adams Road, Forest Road 80 and Forest Road 8040
From Colonial Creek Campground (Thunder Creek Trailhead)
Start at Colonial Creek Campground trailhead on SR 20 mile 130 (elevation 1,060 ft).
From the Copper Glance Trailhead (3,800–3,810 ft, small pullout signboard, parking for roughly 7 cars) on FR 5130 (Eightmile Creek Road), follow Copper Glance Trail #519.

From Winthrop, drive north about 8 miles on West Chewuch Road (County Road 1213) to Eightmile Road (Forest Road 5130), then continue roughly 12-15 miles northwest along Eightmile Creek to the Copper Glance Trailhead (about 3,800-3,810 ft; no fee).

From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east and turn onto Forest Service Road 33; follow roughly 11 miles of gravel road (rough in sections, high-clearance/SUV recommended, sedans passable with care) to its end at the Cougar Divide Trailhead/parking (room for 8-10 vehicles).

Drive to the Crater Creek Trailhead (4,750 ft): from Twisp, take WA-20 east 2 miles to WA-153, then south 12 miles to County Rd 1029/1034 (signed for Foggy Dew Campground) and follow it about 6 miles as it becomes FR 4340 - pavement ends around mile 4 (bear right) - then continue on FR 4340-300 roughly 4.6 more miles to the trailhead parking area (vault toilet, stock ramp, no potable water).

From Twisp, take Highway 20 south ~2 miles to WA-153, then south on WA-153 to County Rd 1029 (Gold Creek Loop), continuing onto County Rd 1034 (Gold Creek Road), which becomes Forest Road 4340 after about 6 miles.

From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 for approximately 28 miles (4.5 miles east of Washington Pass). Turn right on Forest Service Road 400 and follow for 1 mile to the trailhead parking area on the left side of the road.
From the Cutthroat Lake Trailhead (~4,500 ft) on FR-400, 4 miles east of Washington Pass

trailhead: Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
trailheadDirection: Drive SR-20 to Washington Pass and continue west about 1.5 miles to a long, wide pullout beside the highway, which is the climbers' parking. SR-20 closes for winter.

trailhead: Dailey Prairie logging-road gate (Middle Fork Nooksack)
trailheadDirection: From the Middle Fork Nooksack bridge gate: bike the Dailey Prairie logging roads to the north-side climbers' paths (gate status changes year to year — verify before the trip)
From the De Roux trailhead and campground on FR-9737, via the Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 west up the valley to its last switchback
From the Deception Pass Trailhead
Start at the Denny Creek Trailhead (~2,280 ft), reached via Forest Road 58 (Denny Creek Road) off I-90 Exit 47.
From the Denny Creek Trailhead (~2,300 ft) on FR 5830, reached from I-90 Exit 47 by Denny Creek Road (FR 58)

trailhead: Depot Creek Road trailhead (via Chilliwack, BC)
trailheadDirection: From Chilliwack, BC via Chilliwack River Road ~31.7 miles, then the rough Depot Creek Road spur (high-clearance; passport required to cross the border on foot); unmaintained Depot Creek trail up-valley
From the Depot Creek trailhead (reached via the unsigned dirt spur off Chilliwack Lake Road in BC)
From the Depot Creek trailhead parking on the abandoned logging spur off Chilliwack Lake Road (BC) at roughly 2,350 ft

trailhead: Dingford Creek / Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead
trailheadDirection: From I-90 near North Bend, take exit 34, turn left onto 468th Street and follow it to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. Go 12 miles to the large Middle Fork parking area, pass it, and turn right onto a gravel road just after the large concrete bridge, signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Follow it 6 miles over potholes to a gate, with the trailhead just past it.

trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road from North Bend

trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
trailheadDirection: Park at the Dingford Creek Trailhead, where Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FS Road 56) is gated to vehicles; high-clearance is strongly recommended for the potholed last miles.
From US-101 at Brinnon, drive the Dosewallips Road about 8.5 miles to the vehicle road end and park on the roadside.
From the Dosewallips Road (FR-2610) washout parking near Brinnon: road-walk/bike toward the Olympics east-side trails
From the Dosewallips Road (FR-2610) washout parking near Brinnon
From the Dosewallips Road (FR-2610) washout parking near Brinnon: road-walk/bike toward the Olympics east-side trails

trailhead: Downey Creek Trailhead (Trail #768, Suiattle River Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Downey Creek Trailhead (~1,450 ft) on the Suiattle River Road

trailhead: Downey Creek Trailhead (Trail #768, Suiattle River Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Downey Creek Trailhead (~1,450 ft) on the Suiattle River Road, via the Downey Creek / Bachelor Creek approach

trailhead: Downey Creek Trailhead (Trail #768, Suiattle River Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Downey Creek Trailhead (~1,450 ft) on the Suiattle River Road (closed to vehicles at a washout near milepost 4.5; check status)
From US 101 near Brinnon, take Duckabush River Road (FR 2510) west — paved for the first 3.6 miles, then gravel for a total of about 6 miles — to the Duckabush trailhead (FR 2510-060).

From Quilcene, drive US-101 south 15 miles and turn west at the large sign for the Duckabush Recreation Area. Continue about 6 miles (the pavement ends after 3.6 miles, and Collins Campground is near 5 miles), and just past the horse parking area bear right and uphill onto FR-2510-060, which is poorly signed; the trailhead is 0.1 mile up.

From Quilcene, drive south on US-101 about 15 miles to the Duckabush Recreation Area; turn west onto Duckabush River Road/FS Rd 2510 for 6 miles, then follow FS Rd 2510-060 to the Duckabush Trailhead.

Same access as the peak's other routes: via the Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead at the Dingford Creek gate on the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, then about 7.7 miles of closed road east up the valley on foot or by bike
The Eagle Peak Trailhead is about 300 feet past the suspension bridge on the east side of the Nisqually River.
From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east to milepost 138, where the East Bank trailhead parking is beside the highway. SR-20 is closed for winter beyond Colonial Creek.
From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 45 miles and turn right between mileposts 151 and 152 onto the signed Easy Pass road, which leads to the trailhead lot.
From the Easy Pass Trailhead on SR-20 near milepost 151
From the Eightmile Lake Trailhead (~3,300 ft, reached via Icicle Creek Road and Road 7601/Eightmile Road as in the drive note), start on the Eightmile Lake Trail (Trail #1552).

From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme, turn right (east) on Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, and continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which is actually on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12).
Start at the Elbow Lake Trailhead (USFS Trail #697), at the end of FS Road 38 (the Mosquito Lake Road / FS-38 drive from Deming/Acme).
From the Elbow Lake Trailhead ~11 miles up FR-38 off Mosquito Lake Road (road gated Dec 1 - Jun 15 for elk winter range), crossing the Middle Fork Nooksack toward the Green Creek basin

From Marblemount, turn off SR-20 onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles to a large parking area on the right at milepost 20. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel; the road has been closed at this lot for repairs and in winter.

trailhead: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
trailheadDirection: From the Eldorado Creek trailhead lot at mile 20 on Cascade River Road (~2,100 ft)

trailhead: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
trailheadDirection: Drive the Cascade River Road to the Eldorado Creek trailhead (roughly MP 20, ~2,100 ft)

trailhead: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
trailheadDirection: Winter approach: Cascade River Road to the Eldorado Trailhead gate
